name: Nucleotide
oneLine: A single letter of RNA: a sugar, a phosphate and a base.
howItWorks: Every nucleotide has the same sugar and phosphate. What differs is the base: A, U, G or C. Sugars and phosphates link up into a chain, and the bases stick out like letters.
deeper: Chemists have made nucleotides from simple early-Earth ingredients, notably Powner and Sutherland in 2009. Whether that happened the same way in nature is still a leading hypothesis, not a fact.
sizeComparison: a 100,000th the width of a hair
simplification: Each letter gets its own colour and shape. Real bases are all colourless.
